Philips MRI scanners record cardiac, respiratory, and motion signals
alongside the BOLD acquisition via the Physiological Monitoring Unit (PMU).
mrpheus can read these `.log` files, detect QRS complexes with the
Pan-Tompkins algorithm, and compute instantaneous heart rate — producing
cardiac regressors ready for RETROICOR or HRV analysis.

---

## Reading a Philips PMU log

`read_philips_physlog()` parses any Philips PMU `.log` file and returns a
`mrpheus_physlog` object containing the signal matrix, event markers, and
recording metadata.

```r
library(mrpheus)

rec <- read_philips_physlog("sub-01_ses-01_physlog.log")
rec
```

```
## mrpheus Philips PMU recording
## ℹ Path:     sub-01_ses-01_physlog.log
## ℹ System:   wBTU (496 Hz)
## ℹ Channels: v1raw, v2raw, v1, v2, ppu, resp, gx, gy, gz, mark
## ℹ Samples:  4497024 (151.2 min)
## ℹ Markers:  2312 events
```

The `system` argument sets the hardware preset:

```r
# Wireless VCG (Achieva/Ingenia dStream) — default
rec <- read_philips_physlog("sub-01_physlog.log", system = "wBTU")

# Older wired ECG system
rec <- read_philips_physlog("sub-01_physlog.log", system = "wired")

# Site-specific sampling rate
rec <- read_philips_physlog("sub-01_physlog.log", system = "custom", sfreq = 400)
```

The resolved sampling frequency is always available at `rec$HDR$sfreq` so
nothing downstream needs to hardcode it.

### Signal channels

The wBTU layout provides ten channels:

| Channel | Contents |
|---|---|
| `v1raw`, `v2raw` | Raw VCG electrode voltages |
| `v1`, `v2` | Processed VCG signals |
| `ppu` | Peripheral pulse unit (photoplethysmography, foot) |
| `resp` | Respiratory belt |
| `gx`, `gy`, `gz` | 3-axis accelerometer |
| `mark` | Bit-encoded event marker |

```r
# Access signal matrix
head(rec$C)

# Individual channels by name
ecg  <- rec$C[, "v1raw"]
ppu  <- rec$C[, "ppu"]
resp <- rec$C[, "resp"]
```

### Event markers

The `I` element holds 1-based sample indices for each event type:

```r
# Scanner start and stop
rec$I$ScannerStart
rec$I$ScannerStop

# ECG and PPU triggers
rec$I$VcgOnset
rec$I$PpuOnset
```

These are used to align the physiological recording to the fMRI acquisition
window (see [Epoch extraction] below).

---

## QRS detection

`detect_qrs()` implements the Pan-Tompkins (1985) algorithm on any ECG
channel and returns a `mrpheus_qrs` object.

```r
qrs <- detect_qrs(rec$C[, "v1raw"], fs = rec$HDR$sfreq)
qrs
```

```
## mrpheus QRS detection
## ℹ R-peaks detected: 11 432
## ℹ Mean HR:          148 bpm
## ℹ Filter delay:     37 samples (0.075 s)
## ℹ Sampling rate:    496 Hz
```

The algorithm processes the signal in five stages: bandpass filtering
(5–15 Hz), derivative, squaring, 150 ms moving-average integration, and
an adaptive dual-threshold loop with T-wave rejection and search-back for
missed beats.

R-peak indices are stored in `qrs$qrs_i` (1-based, relative to the
bandpass-filtered signal). Account for `qrs$delay` if you need indices
aligned to the raw ECG.

### PPU as an alternative

In neonates, PPU often gives a cleaner signal than the ECG electrodes.
`detect_qrs()` accepts any pulsatile channel:

```r
qrs_ppu <- detect_qrs(rec$C[, "ppu"], fs = rec$HDR$sfreq)
```

---

## Heart rate signal

`compute_hr_signal()` converts R-peak indices into a sample-by-sample
instantaneous HR trace (beats per minute):

```r
hr <- compute_hr_signal(qrs)
```

The function accepts a `mrpheus_qrs` object directly and reads `fs`
from it automatically.

---

## Epoch extraction

To extract the physiology epoch aligned to the fMRI scan, use the
scanner-stop marker. This is more reliable than the start marker because
the exact recording onset varies but the stop is always clean:

```r
sfreq    <- rec$HDR$sfreq
enddelay <- 42       # site-specific: samples between stop marker and scan end
tr       <- 0.392    # fMRI TR in seconds (dHCP neonatal protocol)
vols     <- 2300     # number of volumes

stopidx  <- tail(rec$I$ScannerStop, 1) - enddelay
startidx <- stopidx - round(vols * tr * sfreq)

epoch    <- rec$C[startidx:stopidx, ]   # aligned signal matrix
```

### RR intervals per TR

To get one RR value per volume (for use as a BOLD regressor):

```r
# QRS on epoch only
qrs_epoch <- detect_qrs(epoch[, "v1raw"], fs = sfreq)

# RR intervals (seconds) at each R-peak
rr_s <- diff(qrs_epoch$qrs_i) / sfreq
rr_t <- qrs_epoch$qrs_i[-1] / sfreq

# Interpolate to TR grid
tr_times <- seq(0, vols * tr, by = tr)
rr_tr    <- approx(rr_t, rr_s, xout = tr_times, method = "constant")$y
```

`rr_tr` is a length-`vols` vector ready for inclusion as a nuisance regressor
in a GLM, or as input to RETROICOR phase computation.

---

## HRV across sleep stages

For recordings that include a sleep session alongside fMRI, `detect_qrs()`
provides the R-peak input for `compute_hrv_sleep()` once that function is
fully implemented. The stub currently returns `NA` for all metrics — watch
this space.

---

## Full pipeline

```r
library(mrpheus)

# 1. Read
rec <- read_philips_physlog("sub-01_ses-01_physlog.log")

# 2. Extract scan epoch
sfreq    <- rec$HDR$sfreq
stopidx  <- tail(rec$I$ScannerStop, 1) - 42
startidx <- stopidx - round(2300 * 0.392 * sfreq)
epoch    <- rec$C[startidx:stopidx, ]

# 3. QRS detection
qrs <- detect_qrs(epoch[, "v1raw"], fs = sfreq)

# 4. HR signal
hr  <- compute_hr_signal(qrs)

# 5. RR per TR for BOLD regression
rr_tr <- approx(
  x      = qrs$qrs_i[-1] / sfreq,
  y      = diff(qrs$qrs_i) / sfreq,
  xout   = seq(0, 2300 * 0.392, by = 0.392),
  method = "constant"
)$y
```
